title: Learning Rate & Hyperparameters — Search the Useful Scale
key_insight: Search learning rates and penalties on a logarithmic range, which compares multiplicative changes. Stop weak trials early so compute moves toward promising regions.
body:
## Search the Useful Scale

Testing 0.00011, 0.00012, and 0.00013 wastes trials while ignoring values ten times larger or smaller. Many settings matter by scale.

Search learning rates and penalties on a logarithmic range, which compares multiplicative changes. Stop weak trials early so compute moves toward promising regions.

Population-based methods can change settings during training and copy strong runs. They cost more machinery, so use them only when simpler schedules and careful searches are insufficient.
common_mistakes: The learning rate is the model’s final accuracy.
Hyperparameters are always discovered perfectly without experiments.
Warmup begins with the largest possible update.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Search the Useful Scale” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Good architecture can fail when its training settings make steps unstable, slow, or poorly timed.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Search the Useful Scale” situation, explain Learning Rate & Hyperparameters without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
